items.question: A pea plant carries one 'T' factor and one 't' factor (Tt). What height will it be?
items.explanation: One T is enough for tallness, so Tt plants are tall just like TT plants; only tt plants are short.

items.question: Which pair of sex chromosomes does a human female have?
items.explanation: Women have a matched pair of sex chromosomes, both X; men have one X and one shorter Y.

items.question: One bacterium divides, and both daughter cells divide again. Why do the four bacteria differ only very slightly?
options: They were produced by sexual reproduction
Each received genes from two parents
Small errors happen when DNA is copied
items.explanation: In asexual reproduction the only source of difference is the occasional mistake made while copying DNA, so the offspring are nearly identical.

items.question: According to the chapter, how can a gene control the height of a plant?
options: By carrying information for an enzyme that affects how much growth hormone is made
By deciding how much water the roots absorb
By changing the number of chromosomes in the plant
items.explanation: A gene codes for a protein. If that protein is an enzyme in the pathway that makes a growth hormone, its efficiency decides the hormone level and therefore the height.

items.question: Mendel let the tall F1 plants from a tall x short cross self-pollinate. What did he find in the F2 generation?
options: Every plant was of medium height
About a quarter of the plants were short
Exactly half of the plants were short
items.explanation: Shortness reappeared in roughly one in four F2 plants, showing it had been carried, hidden, by the F1 plants.

items.question: Tall plants with round seeds are crossed with short plants with wrinkled seeds. In the F2, some plants are tall but have wrinkled seeds. What does this show?
options: Height and seed shape are inherited independently of each other
Height and seed shape are always passed on together
A mutation occurred in the F1 plants
items.explanation: A combination that neither parent had can only appear if the factors for height and for seed shape are sorted separately.

items.question: How many sets of genes does each germ cell carry?
items.explanation: Body cells carry two gene sets, one from each parent; a germ cell carries only one so that fertilisation brings the total back to two.

items.question: How much genetic material do the father and the mother each contribute to a child?
options: Most of it comes from the father
Most of it comes from the mother
items.explanation: Both parents give almost the same amount of genetic material, which is why any trait can be shaped by DNA from either side.

items.question: In which of these would you expect to see the least variation among individuals?
items.explanation: Sugarcane plants in a field differ very little from one another, whereas sexually reproducing animals such as humans show clear differences.

items.question: What is a section of DNA that carries the information for one protein called?
items.explanation: A gene is the stretch of DNA holding the instructions for one particular protein; a chromosome is a much larger piece of DNA containing many genes.

items.question: All F1 plants from a tall x short cross are tall, yet some F2 plants are short. What does this tell us about the F1 plants?
options: They carried only the factor for tallness
They carried factors for both tallness and shortness, but only tallness showed
Shortness appeared because of a new mutation
The factor for tallness was lost in the F1
items.explanation: Shortness could only come back in the F2 if the F1 plants carried it; it was hidden because tallness is dominant over it.

items.question: In the F2 generation of Mendel's tall x short cross, what fraction of the plants are tall?
items.explanation: One quarter are short (tt), so the other three quarters (TT and Tt) are tall.

items.question: If each parent passed on its genes as one single, whole unit, why would the round/green x wrinkled/yellow seed experiment not give new combinations?
options: Seed colour would always be green
The number of chromosomes would double
R and y would stay linked and could not be inherited separately
items.explanation: Independent inheritance needs the factors for shape and colour to travel separately; if a whole gene set moved as one unit, R would always go with y.

items.question: A body cell has two copies of every chromosome. Which statement about the chromosomes in a germ cell is correct?
options: It takes both chromosomes of every pair
It takes only the chromosomes that came from the father
It takes one chromosome of each pair, which may be of maternal or paternal origin
It takes only the chromosomes that came from the mother
items.explanation: From each pair a germ cell receives just one chromosome, and for any pair it may be the mother's copy or the father's.

items.question: In human beings, what decides whether a child will be a boy or a girl?
options: Whether the child inherits an X or a Y from the father
Which chromosome the child inherits from the mother
items.explanation: Every child gets an X from the mother, so the father's contribution decides: X gives a girl, Y gives a boy.
